documented_markup_differences.description: CN places quotation marks around the terms for glory and respect; EN omits the matching quotation marks.

documented_meaning_differences.description: CN depicts the Sarkaz warriors as having risen from the civil war; EN describes them as redeployed.
EN adds an explicit acknowledgement before Manfred's unfinished clause; the corresponding words are absent from CN.
documented_meaning_differences.resolution: Russian follows CN and does not add the EN clause.

documented_meaning_differences.description: CN uses a broader term for divisions or estrangement; EN narrows it to prejudices.
CN says books from an entire wall fell; EN says an entire bookshelf was knocked down.
EN adds «fate» to the invisible-tides image; CN does not explicitly include it.
documented_meaning_differences.resolution: Russian follows CN and does not add «судьбы».

documented_meaning_differences.cn: CN uses pronoun 他 for the first person in «他和曼弗雷德都很好».
documented_meaning_differences.en: EN resolves the pronoun explicitly as Theresis.
documented_meaning_differences.resolution: Russian preserves the CN pronoun; its antecedent is established by context.

documented_meaning_differences.cn: CN says the Doctor has become more 冷静 (calm, composed).
documented_meaning_differences.en: EN renders this as more clinical.

documented_meaning_differences.cn: CN says «我们始终是在冒险» — they are continually taking risks.
documented_meaning_differences.en: EN says they have always been in danger.
documented_meaning_differences.resolution: Russian follows CN with «Мы всё время рискуем…».
